aloo-gobi-roti: Knead 1 cup wheat flour with salt and about 1/2 cup water into a soft dough; rest it under a cloth while you cook the sabzi.
Cut 1 small cauliflower (300 g) into florets and 2 potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Chop 1 onion and 1 tomato; mince 3 garlic cloves and 1 tsp ginger.
Heat 2 tbsp mustard oil on medium until it smokes lightly, then lower the heat. Add 1 tsp cumin, then the onion; fry 4 minutes until golden.
Add garlic, ginger, tomato, 1/2 tsp turmeric and salt; cook 3 minutes until soft. Add potato and cauliflower with 1/4 cup water.
Cover and cook on low 12-15 minutes, stirring twice, until a knife slides in easily. Pressure-cooker option: 1 whistle on medium, then switch off.
Roll the dough into 4 rotis and cook on a hot tawa (induction ok, medium-high) 30-40 seconds a side until brown spots appear. Serve with the sabzi.
baingan-bharta-roti: Make roti dough: 1 cup wheat flour, salt and about 1/2 cup water; knead soft and rest 15 minutes.

Rub 1 large brinjal (400 g) with a little oil and slit twice. Roast directly on a gas flame, turning, 10 minutes until skin is charred and flesh is soft. On induction: bake or air-roast in a pan covered, 20 minutes, turning.
Cool 5 minutes, peel off the skin and mash the flesh with a fork.
Heat 2 tbsp oil on medium; fry 1 chopped onion 4 minutes, then 3 garlic cloves, 1 tsp ginger and 1 green chilli for 1 minute.
Add 1 chopped tomato and salt, cook 4 minutes until mushy. Stir in the brinjal and cook 5 minutes on low; finish with chopped coriander.
Roll and cook 4 rotis on a hot tawa, 30-40 seconds a side. Serve with the bharta.
kadhi-pakora-rice: Wash 3/4 cup rice, add 1.5 cups water and salt, pressure-cook 2 whistles on medium (or simmer covered 15 minutes). Rest.
Whisk 1 cup curd, 3 tbsp besan, 1/2 tsp turmeric, salt and 2 cups water until smooth with no lumps.
Make pakora batter: 1/2 cup besan, 1 chopped onion, salt and 3-4 tbsp water, thick. Drop teaspoon-sized balls into 1 cup hot oil on medium and fry 3-4 minutes until golden; drain.
In a pot heat 1 tbsp mustard oil, add 1/2 tsp fenugreek seeds, then 2 garlic cloves and 1 tsp ginger, 30 seconds. Lower heat, pour in the curd mix.
Stir constantly until it boils, then simmer on low 20 minutes, stirring often so it does not split. Add the pakoras for the last 5 minutes.
Serve the kadhi hot over rice.
dal-palak-rice: Wash 1/2 cup toor dal and 3/4 cup rice separately. Pressure-cook the dal with 1.5 cups water, and salt for 4 whistles on medium; cook rice with 1.5 cups water and 2 whistles.
Wash and chop 2 cups spinach. Chop 1 onion, 1 tomato, 3 garlic cloves and 1 tsp ginger.
Heat 1 tbsp ghee, add 1 tsp cumin, then onion; fry 4 minutes. Add garlic, ginger and tomato; cook 3 minutes until soft.
Add spinach and cook 2 minutes just until wilted so it stays green.
Mash the dal, stir it in with 1/2 cup water and salt, and simmer 5 minutes on low.
Serve over rice with a spoon of ghee.
mixed-veg-roti: Knead 1 cup wheat flour with salt and 1/2 cup water; rest 15 minutes.
Chop 1 carrot, 6 beans, 1 potato, 1 cup cauliflower florets; keep 1/2 cup peas. Chop 1 onion, 1 tomato, 3 garlic cloves, 1 tsp ginger.
Heat 2 tbsp oil on medium; fry onion 4 minutes, add garlic and ginger 1 minute, then tomato and salt; cook 3 minutes.
Add all vegetables and 1/2 cup water. Cover and cook on low 15 minutes, or pressure-cook 1 whistle then switch off.
Roll and cook 4 rotis on a hot tawa, 30-40 seconds a side.
Serve the sabzi with rotis and 1/2 cup cold curd on the side.
gobi-paratha: Grate 1 cup cauliflower fine and squeeze out water in a clean cloth. Mix with 1 tsp grated ginger, 1 chopped green chilli, 1/2 tsp ajwain and salt.
Knead 1.5 cups wheat flour with salt, 1 tsp oil and about 3/4 cup water into soft dough; rest 10 minutes.
Divide dough into 4 balls. Roll each to a small disc, put 2 tbsp filling in the centre, seal and roll gently to 15 cm.
Cook on a hot tawa (medium-high) 1 minute, flip, spread 1/2 tsp butter, flip again and cook 1 minute until golden spots appear.
Serve hot with 1/2 cup curd and a little butter on top.
paneer-paratha: Crumble 100 g paneer. Mix with 1 chopped green chilli, 2 tbsp chopped coriander and salt.
Knead 1.5 cups wheat flour with salt and about 3/4 cup water; rest 10 minutes.
Make 4 balls, flatten, put 2 tbsp filling in each, pinch closed and roll gently to 15 cm without letting filling escape.
Cook on a hot tawa on medium-high 1 minute, flip, smear 1/2 tsp ghee, cook both sides until golden-brown.
masoor-dal-rice: Wash 1/2 cup red lentils and 3/4 cup rice separately. Cook rice with 1.5 cups water, 2 whistles on medium (or simmer covered 15 minutes).
Boil the lentils with 2 cups water, 1/2 tsp turmeric and salt, partly covered, 15 minutes on medium (or 3 whistles in a cooker). Mash lightly.
Chop 1 onion, 1 tomato and 3 garlic cloves. Heat 1 tbsp mustard oil until it smokes lightly, then cool 20 seconds.
Add 1 tsp cumin, garlic, then onion; fry 4 minutes golden. Add tomato and cook 3 minutes.
Pour the tarka into the dal and simmer 3 minutes.
Slice 1/2 cucumber, 1/2 onion and tomato for the salad with a pinch of salt. Serve dal over rice.
aloo-matar-roti: Knead 1 cup wheat flour with salt and about 1/2 cup water; rest 15 minutes.
Chop 2 potatoes into cubes; chop 1 onion, 1 tomato, 3 garlic cloves and 1 tsp ginger.
Heat 2 tbsp oil on medium, add 1 tsp cumin, then onion; fry 4 minutes. Add garlic and ginger, then tomato and salt; cook 4 minutes until oily.
Add potatoes, 3/4 cup peas and 3/4 cup water. Cover and cook 12-15 minutes on low, or 2 whistles in a cooker on medium; mash a few pieces to thicken.
Cook 4 rotis on a hot tawa, 30-40 seconds a side. Serve.
kadai-paneer-roti: Knead 1 cup wheat flour with salt and water; rest 15 minutes. Cut 150 g paneer and 1 capsicum into 2 cm cubes; chop 1 onion, 2 tomatoes, 3 garlic cloves, 1 tsp ginger.
Dry-roast 1 tsp coriander seeds in a pan 1 minute on low, then crush coarsely.
Heat 1 tbsp butter in a kadai on medium; fry onion 4 minutes, add garlic and ginger 1 minute, then tomatoes and salt; cook 6 minutes until mushy.
Add crushed coriander and 1/4 cup water. Add capsicum and cook 3 minutes, keeping it crunchy.
Add paneer and 2 tbsp cream; simmer 2 minutes on low, do not boil hard.
Cook 4 rotis on a hot tawa. Serve with the paneer.
puri-aloo: Knead 1 cup wheat flour with 1 tbsp oil, salt and about 1/3 cup water into a stiff dough; rest 15 minutes.
Boil 2 potatoes (3 whistles in a cooker on medium), peel and crush roughly.
Heat 1 tbsp oil, add 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp ginger, 1 green chilli and 1 chopped tomato; cook 4 minutes. Add potatoes, salt and 1/2 cup water; simmer 5 minutes.
Roll dough into 8 small discs, 8 cm wide.
Heat 2 cups oil in a kadai to medium-high (a pinch of dough should rise in 5 seconds). Slide in a puri and press gently so it puffs; fry 30 seconds a side until golden. Drain on paper.
Serve hot puris with the aloo sabzi.
litti-chokha: Knead 1 cup wheat flour with 1 tbsp ghee, ajwain, salt and water into a firm dough. Mix 1/3 cup sattu with 1 tsp chopped ginger, 1 chopped garlic clove, 1/2 chopped onion, 1 tsp mustard oil and salt, with a splash of water.

Stuff each of 4 dough balls with 1 tbsp sattu mix, seal, and bake in a preheated 200 C oven for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until brown and cracked. Pan option: cook covered on low induction 20 minutes, turning often.
Meanwhile roast 1 brinjal, 1 tomato and 1 potato (boiled first, 3 whistles) on a flame or in a pan until charred; peel.
Mash them with 1 chopped onion, 1 garlic clove, 1 green chilli, salt and 1 tbsp mustard oil to make the chokha.
Dunk the hot littis in melted ghee and serve with the chokha.
sattu-paratha: Mix 1/3 cup sattu with 1/2 chopped onion, 2 minced garlic cloves, 1 tsp ginger, 1 green chilli, 1/2 tsp ajwain, 1 tsp mustard oil, salt and a splash of water into a crumbly filling.
Knead 1.5 cups wheat flour with salt and about 3/4 cup water; rest 10 minutes.
Roll 4 balls into small discs, fill with 2 tbsp sattu, seal and roll to 15 cm.
Cook on a medium-high tawa 1 minute, flip, brush with mustard oil, and cook both sides until golden.
thalipeeth: Mix 1 cup bhajani flour with 1 chopped onion, 2 tbsp chopped coriander, 1 chopped green chilli, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tbsp sesame seeds and salt.
Add about 1/2 cup warm water and knead a soft, slightly sticky dough; divide in 4.
Heat a tawa on medium and grease with 1 tsp oil. Wet your fingers and pat one ball flat directly on the tawa to 12 cm; poke 3 holes.
Drizzle 1/2 tsp oil in the holes and edges; cover and cook 2 minutes, flip, cook 2 minutes until crisp and brown.
Repeat and serve with 1/2 cup curd.
vada-pav: Boil 3 potatoes (3 whistles on medium), cool, peel and mash coarsely.
Heat 1 tbsp oil, add 1 tsp mustard seeds, 8 curry leaves, 1 tbsp chopped garlic, 1 tsp ginger and 1 green chilli; fry 1 minute. Mix into potatoes with salt and shape 4 balls.
Whisk 1/2 cup besan, salt and about 1/3 cup water into a thick batter.
Heat 2 cups oil on medium-high; dip each ball in batter and fry 3-4 minutes until golden, turning. Drain.
Split 4 pav, rub with garlic if you like, tuck a vada inside and press. Serve hot.
pithla-bhakri: Make bhakri dough: mix 1 cup jowar flour with salt and about 1/2 cup hot water; knead quickly with wet hands while warm. Pat 2 bhakris 12 cm wide by hand, cook on a tawa on medium 2 minutes a side, then puff 30 seconds on direct flame (or press with a cloth on the tawa if induction).
Mix 1/2 cup besan with 1 cup water, salt and 1/4 tsp turmeric into a smooth, lump-free slurry.
Heat 1 tbsp oil, add 1 tsp mustard seeds, then 1 chopped onion, 2 garlic cloves and 1 green chilli; fry 4 minutes.
Pour in the slurry, stirring constantly; cook on medium-low 6-8 minutes until thick like porridge.
Serve hot pithla with the bhakri.
varan-bhat: Wash 1/2 cup toor dal and 3/4 cup rice separately. Pressure-cook the dal with 1.5 cups water, 1/4 tsp turmeric, a pinch of hing and salt for 4 whistles on medium.
Cook the rice with 1.5 cups water and salt, 2 whistles (or simmer covered 15 minutes).
Mash the dal, add 1 tsp jaggery and 1/2 cup hot water; simmer 3 minutes.
Add a squeeze of lemon (about 1 tsp) and mix.
Serve the dal over rice with 1 tbsp ghee on top and a lemon wedge.
puran-poli: Pressure-cook 1/2 cup chana dal with 1.5 cups water, 3 whistles on medium; drain well (keep the water for another use).
Cook the dal with 1/2 cup grated jaggery in a pan on low 8-10 minutes, stirring, until thick and dry. Mash smooth, add 1/2 tsp cardamom and a pinch of nutmeg; cool and make 6 balls.
Knead 1 cup wheat flour with 1 tbsp ghee, salt and water into a soft dough; rest 20 minutes.
Flatten a dough ball, stuff with a filling ball, seal, and roll gently to 15 cm with dry flour.
Cook on a medium tawa 1-2 minutes a side with 1/2 tsp ghee until golden. Serve warm with ghee.
undhiyu: Chop 1 cup surti papdi, 1 raw banana, 1 sweet potato, 1 small purple yam, 1 potato and 1 small brinjal into big pieces; slit the brinjal and keep other pieces in water.
Grind 1/2 cup grated coconut, 2 tbsp peanuts, 1 tbsp sesame seeds, 3 garlic cloves, 1 tsp ginger and 2 green chillies coarsely with salt and a little water.
Make muthia-style dumplings: mix 1/3 cup besan with a spoon of the paste, salt and 1 tbsp oil; shape small balls.
Heat 3 tbsp oil in a heavy pot; add the vegetables with the paste and salt and mix well. Add 1/2 cup water.
Cover tightly and cook on low 35-40 minutes, stirring gently only twice. Add the besan balls for the last 10 minutes. (Pressure-cooker: 2 whistles then simmer 10 minutes.)
Knead 1 cup wheat flour into dough, roll and fry 4 puris in hot oil; serve with undhiyu.
gujarati-dal-bhat: Wash 1/2 cup toor dal and 3/4 cup rice. Pressure-cook the dal with 2 cups water and salt for 4 whistles on medium; cook rice with 1.5 cups water, 2 whistles.
Knead 1/2 cup wheat flour with salt and water; roll and cook 3 thin rotlis on a hot tawa.
Make shaak: heat 1 tbsp oil, add 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, ginger and a green chilli, then 1.5 cups cubed bottle gourd, 1 chopped tomato, salt and 1/4 cup water; cook covered 10 minutes.
Mash dal, add 1 tbsp jaggery, 2 pieces of kokum, 1 tbsp peanuts and 1/2 cup water; simmer 8 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp ghee with 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, pour over the dal.
Serve dal, rice, shaak and rotli together.
handvo: Soak 1/2 cup rice, 2 tbsp chana dal, 2 tbsp toor dal and 2 tbsp urad dal for 5 hours; grind coarsely with 1/3 cup curd, ferment 8 hours or overnight.
Grate 1 cup bottle gourd, squeeze lightly and fold into the batter with 1 tsp grated ginger, 1 chopped green chilli, 1 tbsp sesame seeds and salt.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a nonstick pan, add 1 tsp mustard seeds and 1 tsp sesame seeds, pour in the batter and level it.
Cover and cook on low 12 minutes until the base is crisp and golden; flip carefully and cook 10 minutes more. A skewer should come out clean.
Cut into wedges and serve with chutney (grind 2 tbsp curd or coconut with a green chilli if desired).
khandvi: Whisk 1/2 cup besan, 1 cup buttermilk, 1/2 cup water, 1 tsp grated ginger, 1 chopped green chilli, a pinch of hing and salt until smooth.
Cook on low-medium, stirring non-stop, 8-10 minutes until very thick and it leaves the pan.
Spread a spoonful quickly on a greased plate; if it spreads thin and sets in 1 minute it is ready. Spread the rest on 2-3 greased plates or the back of a steel tray, thin as possible.
Cut each sheet into 4 cm strips and roll them up.
Heat 1 tbsp oil, crackle 1 tsp mustard seeds and 1 tsp sesame seeds, pour over the rolls.
Top with 2 tbsp grated coconut and chopped coriander.
dal-baati-churma: Mix 2 cups wheat flour with 4 tbsp ghee, salt and about 3/4 cup water into a firm dough. Shape 8 balls, press a dent in each. Bake at 200 C 30-35 minutes, turning once until cracked and brown (pan option: covered on low induction 30 minutes, turning).
Mix 3 tbsp each toor, chana, moong and urad dal (1/2 cup total); wash and pressure-cook with 2.5 cups water and salt for 5 whistles on medium; mash.
Heat 1 tbsp ghee, add 1 tsp cumin, 1 chopped onion, 3 garlic cloves, 1 tsp ginger and 1 tomato; cook 7 minutes. Stir into the dal and simmer 5 minutes.
Churma: crush 2 hot baatis, mix with 2 tbsp ghee and 3 tbsp grated jaggery.
Break the remaining baatis, drench in ghee and serve with the dal and churma.
gatte-sabzi-roti: Knead 1 cup wheat flour with salt and water; rest 15 minutes.
Mix 1 cup besan with 1 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp crushed coriander seeds, 1/2 tsp red chilli, salt and 2-3 tbsp water into a stiff dough. Roll into fingers 1.5 cm thick.
Boil the gatte in 3 cups simmering water 10-12 minutes until they float; lift out, cut into pieces; save 1/2 cup water.
Whisk 1/2 cup curd with 1/2 tsp turmeric. Heat 1 tbsp ghee, add a pinch of hing, 1 tsp ginger and 1 green chilli, then add curd on low heat and stir constantly 4 minutes.
Add the gatte and saved water; simmer 5 minutes. Cook 4 rotis on a tawa and serve.
bisi-bele-bath: Wash 1/2 cup rice and 1/4 cup toor dal. Chop 1 carrot, 6 beans, 1/2 cup peas and 1 onion.

Pressure-cook rice, dal and vegetables with 3 cups water, 1 tbsp tamarind pulp, salt and 2 tbsp bisi bele bath powder, 4 whistles on medium. Mash well; add 1/2 cup hot water for a porridge consistency.
Simmer the mash 5 minutes with 2 tbsp grated coconut.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee; fry 1 tbsp cashews golden 1 minute, add 8 curry leaves for 10 seconds.
Pour over the bisi bele bath and serve hot with boondi or crisp snacks.
akki-roti: Mix 1 cup rice flour with 1 chopped onion, 2 tbsp chopped dill, 1 chopped green chilli, 1 tsp cumin, 8 chopped curry leaves, 2 tbsp grated coconut and salt.
Add about 1/3 cup warm water and knead a soft dough.
Grease a tawa on medium; place a ball of dough and pat thin with wet fingers to 14 cm. Make a few holes.
Drizzle 1/2 tsp oil, cover and cook 2 minutes, flip, cook 2 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Chutney: grind 1/2 cup coconut, 1 green chilli, salt and 1/4 cup water. Serve with the roti.
neer-dosa: Soak 3/4 cup rice 3 hours. Drain and grind with 1/4 cup grated coconut, salt and about 1.5 cups water to a very thin, pourable batter.
Heat a nonstick tawa on medium and rub with a little oil.
Stir the batter, pour from a height to cover the pan thinly; it will be lacy. Cover and cook 1 minute; do not flip.
Fold in half and lift; make 4 dosas.
Grind 1/2 cup coconut, 1 green chilli, 1 tsp ginger, salt and 1/4 cup water for chutney. Serve.
tomato-pappu-rice: Wash 1/2 cup toor dal and 3/4 cup rice. Pressure-cook dal with 1.5 cups water, 1/2 tsp turmeric and 2 chopped tomatoes 4 whistles on medium; cook rice 2 whistles.
Mash the dal. Add salt and 1/2 cup water and simmer 3 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp ghee, add 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 sliced onion, 2 garlic cloves, 1 green chilli and 8 curry leaves; fry 3 minutes.
Add the tadka to the pappu.
Serve over rice with 1 tbsp ghee.
gutti-vankaya-rice: Cook 3/4 cup rice with 1.5 cups water, 2 whistles. Slit 4 small brinjals into 4 without cutting through the stem; keep in water.
Dry-roast 2 tbsp peanuts, 1 tbsp sesame seeds, 2 tbsp coconut, 2 red chillies on low 3 minutes; grind with 1 onion, 3 garlic cloves and 1 tsp ginger and a little water to a paste; salt.
Stuff the brinjal slits with some paste.
Heat 2 tbsp oil, add the stuffed brinjals and cook covered on low 8 minutes, turning gently.
Add the rest of paste, 1 tbsp tamarind pulp and 3/4 cup water; simmer covered 10 minutes until the oil floats.
uttapam: Soak 3/4 cup rice and 1/4 cup urad dal 5 hours, grind and ferment overnight with salt (or use 1.5 cups ready batter).
Chop 1 onion, 1 tomato, 1 green chilli and coriander finely.
Heat a tawa on medium, grease lightly, pour a ladle of batter and spread 10 cm thick.
Scatter the vegetables on top and press lightly; drizzle 1/2 tsp oil, cover and cook 3 minutes, flip, cook 2 minutes.
Grind 1/2 cup coconut, 1 green chilli, 1 tsp ginger, salt and 1/4 cup water for chutney. Serve.
meen-curry-kerala: Wash 3/4 cup rice and cook with 1.5 cups water, 2 whistles. Wash 300 g fish pieces in clean water, pat dry, rub with salt and 1/4 tsp turmeric; keep refrigerated until use.
Grind 1/2 cup grated coconut, 4 shallots, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp ginger and 2 tsp red chilli with 1/2 cup water.
Heat 1 tbsp coconut oil in an earthen pot or pan, add 8 curry leaves, then the paste, 1 cup water, 2 pieces kudampuli (soaked 5 minutes) and salt; simmer 5 minutes on medium.
Add the fish; cook covered on low 8-10 minutes without stirring (shake pan). Fish is done when opaque and flakes easily, with no translucent centre.
Finish with 1 tsp raw coconut oil. Wash hands, board and knife with hot soapy water after handling raw fish; eat within 2 hours.
puttu-kadala: Soak 1/2 cup black chickpeas overnight. Pressure-cook with salt and 2 cups water, 5 whistles on medium.

Mix 1 cup rice flour with 1/4 cup water and salt, rubbing until it holds when pressed and crumbles when touched. Fill a puttu maker alternating layers of 2 tbsp coconut and flour; steam 7-8 minutes on high until steam shows.
Heat 1 tbsp coconut oil, crackle 1 tsp mustard seeds, then fry 4 sliced shallots, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp ginger and 8 curry leaves for 4 minutes.
Add the cooked chickpeas with their water and 2 tbsp coconut; mash a few and simmer 8 minutes.
cabbage-thoran-rice: Wash 1/2 cup toor dal and 3/4 cup rice; pressure-cook dal with 2 cups water, salt and 1 chopped tomato for 4 whistles; rice 2 whistles.
Make sambar: mash dal, add 1 tbsp tamarind pulp and 1/2 cup water; simmer 8 minutes; temper with 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 4 curry leaves and 1 tsp coconut oil.
Chop 2 cups cabbage finely. Grind 1/4 cup coconut, 2 shallots, 1 garlic clove and 1 green chilli coarsely.
Heat 1 tbsp coconut oil, add 1 tsp mustard seeds and 8 curry leaves, then cabbage and salt. Cook uncovered on medium 5 minutes.
Add the coconut mix, cook 2 minutes more.
Serve thoran with rice and sambar.
parotta-egg-roast: Knead 1 cup maida with salt, 1 tbsp oil and water into a soft dough; rest 1 hour. Divide into 4 balls, flatten, oil, stretch thin, pleat, coil and rest 10 minutes.
Roll each coil flat and cook on a hot tawa on medium-high 2 minutes a side until layered; clap together to flake.
Hard-boil 3 eggs (10 minutes in boiling water), cool, peel, and slit lightly.
Heat 1 tbsp coconut oil, fry 1 tsp fennel, 8 curry leaves, 2 sliced onions 6 minutes; add 3 garlic cloves, 1 tsp ginger, 2 tomatoes, 1 tsp red chilli and salt; cook 8 minutes until oily.
Add the eggs with 1/4 cup water, cook 3 minutes; eggs must be fully set, with firm yolks. Wash hands after handling shells.
chicken-chettinad-rice: Cook 3/4 cup rice with 1.5 cups water, 2 whistles. Wash hands, then cut 300 g chicken into pieces and keep it chilled until use.
Dry-roast 1/4 cup coconut, 1 tsp fennel, 1 tsp black pepper and 2 red chillies for 2 minutes on low; grind with a little water.
Heat 2 tbsp oil; fry 2 chopped onions 6 minutes, then 4 garlic cloves, 1 tsp ginger and 8 curry leaves for 1 minute. Add 2 tomatoes and salt, cook 5 minutes.
Add the chicken and ground paste; cook 5 minutes, add 1 cup water.
Pressure-cook 3 whistles on medium or simmer covered 20 minutes. Chicken is done when no pink remains and juices run clear (75 C inside).
Wash board, knife and hands with hot soapy water after raw chicken; serve with rice.
goan-fish-curry-rice: Cook 3/4 cup rice with 1.5 cups water, 2 whistles. Wash 300 g fish, pat dry, rub with salt and 1/4 tsp turmeric; keep chilled.
Grind 1/2 cup grated coconut, 1 onion, 3 garlic cloves, 1 tsp ginger and 3 red chillies with 1/2 cup water to a smooth paste.
Heat 1 tbsp coconut oil, add the paste and fry on medium 5 minutes. Add 1 cup water, 1 tbsp tamarind pulp, 2 kokum pieces and salt; simmer 8 minutes.
Add the fish; cook covered on low 8-10 minutes without stirring. Fish is done when opaque and flaking easily.
Wash hands, knife and board after raw fish; serve with rice.
pork-vindaloo-rice: Cook 3/4 cup rice with 1.5 cups water, 2 whistles. Cut 300 g pork into 3 cm cubes; keep chilled.
Grind 3 red chillies, 1 tsp cumin, 1 small stick cinnamon, 3 cloves, 4 garlic cloves, 1 tsp ginger, 1 tbsp tamarind and 2 tbsp vinegar into a paste.
Marinate pork with the paste and salt for at least 30 minutes, ideally 4 hours chilled.
Heat 2 tbsp oil, fry 2 sliced onions 6 minutes golden, add pork with marinade and cook 6 minutes, stirring.
Add 1/2 cup water; pressure-cook 6-8 whistles on medium until tender, or simmer covered 50 minutes. Pork must be cooked through (no pink, 70 C inside).
Simmer uncovered 5 minutes to thicken. Wash board, knife and hands after raw pork; serve with rice.
masor-tenga-rice: Cook 3/4 cup rice with 1.5 cups water, 2 whistles. Wash 300 g fish, pat dry, rub with salt and 1/4 tsp turmeric; keep chilled.
Heat 1 tbsp mustard oil until it smokes, lower the heat, and shallow-fry the fish 2 minutes a side; set aside.
In the same oil add 1/4 tsp fenugreek seeds, then 3 garlic cloves and 1 tsp ginger for 30 seconds. Add 2 chopped tomatoes, 1/4 tsp turmeric and salt; cook 6 minutes.
Add 1.5 cups water, simmer 5 minutes, then slip in the fish. Cook covered 5 minutes on low; fish should flake easily and be opaque.
Switch off, squeeze in juice of 1/2 lemon, add chopped coriander. Wash hands and board after raw fish. Serve with rice.
veg-momos: Mix 1 cup maida with salt, 1 tsp oil and about 1/3 cup water into a firm dough; rest 20 minutes covered.
Finely chop 1 cup cabbage, 1/2 carrot, 1 onion, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp ginger and 1 spring onion. Salt and squeeze out water; add 1 tsp soy sauce and 1 tsp sesame oil.
Roll dough into 12 thin discs (8 cm), put 1 tbsp filling in each, and pleat closed.
Grease a steamer plate and steam over boiling water 10-12 minutes on high until the wrappers look glossy.
Chutney: blend 3 red chillies (soaked 10 minutes in hot water), 2 garlic cloves, 1/2 tsp ginger, salt and 1 tsp soy sauce. Serve hot.
rogan-josh-rice: Cook 3/4 cup rice with 1.5 cups water, 2 whistles. Cut 300 g mutton into pieces; keep chilled.
Heat 2 tbsp mustard oil until smoking, lower the heat, and brown the mutton 8 minutes in batches.
Add 2 sliced onions, 4 garlic cloves, 1 tsp ginger; fry 6 minutes. Add 2 tsp Kashmiri chilli, 1 tsp fennel, 1/2 tsp dry ginger, 2 cardamoms, 3 cloves and salt with 2 tbsp water; cook 3 minutes.
Take off the heat, whisk in 1/2 cup curd, return to low heat and stir 2 minutes.
Add 1.5 cups water; pressure-cook 8-10 whistles on medium or simmer covered 60 minutes until the meat is tender and cooked through.
Finish with 1 tsp ghee. Wash board, hands and knife after raw meat; serve with rice.
haak-rice: Cook 3/4 cup rice with 1.5 cups water, 2 whistles.
Wash 300 g collard greens, remove thick stems, and chop.
Heat 1 tbsp mustard oil until it smokes lightly, add a pinch of asafoetida, 2 chopped garlic cloves and 1 chopped onion; fry 3 minutes.
Add 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli, the greens, salt and 1/2 cup water; cover and cook 10 minutes on medium, then uncover and cook 5 minutes until the water has gone.
dalma-rice: Wash 1/2 cup toor dal and 3/4 cup rice. Pressure-cook dal with 2 cups water, 1/2 tsp turmeric and salt for 4 whistles; cook the rice with 1.5 cups water, 2 whistles.
Chop 1 cup pumpkin, 1 raw banana, 1 brinjal and 1 potato into big cubes.
Add the vegetables and 1/2 cup water to the mashed dal; simmer 10 minutes on low until soft.
Heat 1 tbsp mustard oil, add 1 tsp cumin and 1 tsp grated ginger; pour onto the dalma.
Top with 2 tbsp grated coconut and serve with rice.
pakhala-bhata: Use 1.5 cups of rice cooked the night before and soaked in water; keep covered in a cool place for 8-12 hours. Use it within a day only if kept refrigerated and smelling pleasantly sour, discard if it smells off.
For badi chura: fry 6 urad dal badi in 1 tbsp mustard oil on medium 2 minutes until golden; crush with 1 boiled potato, 1/2 chopped onion, 1 green chilli and salt.
Stir salt, 2 tbsp curd and 1/2 tsp roasted cumin into the rice and water.
Add 6 chopped mint leaves, lemon juice and chopped onion on top.
Serve cold with the badi chura.
pani-puri: Make puri dough: mix 1/2 cup semolina, 2 tbsp wheat flour, a pinch of salt and about 3 tbsp water; knead stiff, rest 20 minutes. Roll thin and cut 16 small circles with a lid.
Heat 2 cups oil on medium-high; fry the puris pressing so they puff, 1 minute until golden. Drain and cool.
Boil 2 potatoes and 1/2 cup soaked chickpeas (4 whistles). Mash lightly with salt and 1/2 tsp cumin.
Grind 1 cup mint, 2 green chillies, 1 tsp ginger, 1 tsp cumin, black salt and 2 cups water; strain. Mix 2 tbsp tamarind pulp with 1 tbsp jaggery for sweet water.
Fill each puri with the potato mix and pour in the pani. Eat immediately.
bhel-puri: Chop 1 onion, 1 tomato, 1 boiled potato, 1/2 raw mango, 1 green chilli and coriander finely.
Dry-roast 2 tbsp peanuts 2 minutes on low in a pan; cool.
In a big bowl mix 2 cups puffed rice with the vegetables, peanuts and 1 tsp salt.
Add 1 tbsp tamarind chutney, 1 tbsp mint chutney (mint ground with green chilli) and 1 tsp garlic chutney.
Toss gently, top with 2 tbsp sev and coriander and eat at once so it stays crunchy. No cooking needed except for the peanuts.
dahi-vada: Soak 1/2 cup urad dal for 4 hours; grind with 2-3 tbsp water into a thick, fluffy batter. Add salt, 1 tsp ginger and 1 green chilli; whisk 2 minutes.
Heat 2 cups oil on medium; drop spoonfuls of batter in and fry 4 minutes until golden; drain.
Soak vadas in warm salted water 10 minutes, press gently to squeeze out water.
Whisk 1.5 cups curd with salt until smooth; mix 2 tbsp tamarind pulp with 2 tbsp water.
Layer vadas with curd; top with tamarind, 1/2 tsp roasted cumin and black salt. Chill and serve.
aloo-tikki-chaat: Boil 3 potatoes (3 whistles on medium), cool, peel, mash. Soak 2 bread slices in water for 10 seconds, squeeze and add with salt, 1 tsp ginger and 1 green chilli; knead and make 4 patties.
Boil 1/2 cup chickpeas (soaked overnight) 4 whistles; keep warm.
Heat 2 tbsp oil on a tawa on medium; shallow-fry tikkis 3-4 minutes a side until crisp.
Whisk 1/2 cup curd with salt. Mix 2 tbsp tamarind pulp with water; blend mint with green chilli for chutney.
Top the tikkis with chickpeas, curd, chutneys, chopped onion and 1/2 tsp chaat masala.
kachori-sabzi: Soak 1/2 cup moong dal 2 hours, drain and grind coarse. Roast with 1 tsp fennel, a pinch of hing, 1 green chilli, 1 tsp ginger and salt in 1 tbsp oil on low 4 minutes until dry; cool.
Knead 1 cup maida with 2 tbsp oil, salt and water into a firm dough; rest 20 minutes.
Make 6 balls, flatten, fill each with 1 tbsp stuffing, seal and press flat.
Fry in 2 cups oil on low-medium 6-8 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp.
Sabzi: boil 2 potatoes (3 whistles); sauté 1 chopped tomato, 1 tsp ginger and hing in 1 tbsp oil 4 minutes; add potatoes, salt and 3/4 cup water, simmer 8 minutes. Serve.
masala-omelette: Chop 1 small onion, 1/2 tomato, 1 green chilli and a handful of coriander finely.
Crack 3 eggs into a bowl and whisk with salt and the chopped mix.
Heat 1 tsp butter on a nonstick pan on medium; pour in the egg mix and spread it.
Cook 2 minutes, flip and cook 1-2 minutes until the egg is fully set and not runny. Wash hands after handling raw egg.
Toast 2 bread slices on the pan with 1/2 tsp butter and serve with the omelette.
anda-paratha: Knead 1 cup wheat flour with salt, 1 tsp oil and about 1/2 cup water into soft dough; rest 10 minutes. Make 2 balls and roll thin to 18 cm.
Whisk 2 eggs with 1/2 chopped onion, 1 green chilli, coriander and salt.
Cook a paratha on a medium-high tawa 1 minute, flip, brush with oil.
Pour half the egg on top, spread; flip when set, 1 minute, and cook 1 minute until the egg is fully cooked, no wet patches. Wash hands after handling raw eggs.
jeera-rice-dal: Wash 3/4 cup rice and 1/2 cup moong dal separately. Soak rice 15 minutes.
Pressure-cook dal with 2 cups water, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp ginger and salt for 3 whistles on medium; mash.
Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a pot, add 1 tsp cumin, then drained rice; stir 1 minute. Add 1.5 cups water and salt; cook covered on low 12 minutes or pressure-cook 2 whistles.
Temper the dal with 1/2 tbsp ghee and 1/2 tsp cumin; add chopped coriander.
rice-kheer: Wash 1/4 cup rice and soak 20 minutes; drain.
Boil 2 cups milk in a heavy pot on medium; add rice and lower to low.
Simmer 25-30 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes and scraping the base, until the rice is soft and the milk thickens.
Add 3 tbsp sugar and 1/4 tsp crushed cardamom; cook 3 minutes.
Add chopped almonds and pistachios. Serve warm or chilled.
suji-halwa: Heat 3 tbsp ghee in a pan on low. Fry 1 tbsp cashews and 1 tbsp raisins 1 minute; set aside.
Add 1/2 cup semolina and roast on low 6-8 minutes, stirring, until fragrant and light golden.
Meanwhile boil 1.5 cups water with 1/3 cup sugar and 1/4 tsp cardamom.
Pour the hot syrup carefully into the semolina (it splutters), stirring continuously.
Cook 2-3 minutes until thick and ghee separates; top with fried cashews and raisins.
gajar-halwa: Grate 500 g carrots. Pressure-cook with 1 cup milk, 1 whistle on medium, or cook in a pot 15 minutes.
Cook uncovered on medium, stirring, 15-20 minutes until the milk has evaporated.
Add 2 tbsp ghee and cook 8 minutes until the carrots turn deep red.
Add 1/3 cup sugar; the mixture releases water, so cook 8 minutes until thick.
Stir in 1/4 cup crumbled khoya, 1/2 tsp cardamom, chopped almonds and cashews; cook 3 minutes. Serve warm.
sweet-lassi: Chill 1 cup curd and 1/2 cup milk.
Add curd, milk, 2 tbsp sugar, 1/4 tsp cardamom and 2 tbsp cold water to a blender.
Blend 1 minute until frothy; taste and adjust sugar.
Pour into 2 glasses and serve cold. No heating needed.
masala-chai: Bring 1 cup water to a boil in a pan on medium.
Add 1 tsp crushed ginger and 2 crushed cardamom pods; boil 2 minutes.
Add 2 tsp tea leaves and 2 tsp sugar; boil 1 minute.
Pour in 1 cup milk, bring to a rolling boil, then reduce and simmer 2 minutes on low.
Strain into 2 cups and serve with biscuits.
tomato-soup: Chop 4 tomatoes, 1 onion, 1 carrot, 2 garlic cloves and 1 tsp ginger.
Melt 1 tbsp butter in a pot on medium; cook onion, garlic, ginger and carrot 4 minutes.
Add tomatoes, salt and 1.5 cups water; simmer covered 12 minutes (or 3 whistles in a cooker).
Cool 5 minutes, blend smooth, and strain if you like.
Return to heat, add 1/4 tsp black pepper, simmer 3 minutes. Toast 2 bread slices with butter and serve.
bombay-sandwich: Boil 2 potatoes and 1 beetroot (4 whistles on medium); cool, peel and slice thin. Slice cucumber, tomato and onion.
Butter 4 bread slices on one side; spread green chutney on the other side of 2 slices.
Layer potato, beetroot, cucumber, tomato and onion on the chutney slices; sprinkle with salt, add grated cheese and close.
Grill in a sandwich maker 4 minutes, or on a medium tawa with butter 2-3 minutes a side, until golden.
Cut into triangles and serve hot.
ragi-mudde-saaru: Wash 1/4 cup toor dal; pressure-cook with 1.5 cups water, salt, 2 chopped tomatoes and 1 chopped onion for 4 whistles on medium.
Add 1 cup chopped spinach, 2 garlic cloves and 1 tbsp tamarind pulp; simmer 8 minutes. Temper with 1 tsp oil, 1/2 tsp mustard seeds and 6 curry leaves.
Boil 1.5 cups water with salt. Reduce heat to low; sprinkle in 1/2 cup ragi flour, cook 2 minutes without stirring, then mix hard with a wooden spoon to smooth.
Cover and cook 3 minutes; wet your hands and shape into 4 balls.
rava-idli: Dry-roast 1 cup semolina on low 3 minutes until fragrant; cool.
Heat 1 tbsp oil, crackle 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, fry 1 tbsp cashews and 1 tsp ginger 1 minute; mix into semolina.
Add 3/4 cup curd, salt and about 1/2 cup water to make a thick batter; rest 15 minutes.
Fill greased idli moulds and steam 10-12 minutes on high until a knife comes out clean.
Sambar: pressure-cook 1/2 cup toor dal with 1.5 cups water, 3 whistles; add chopped onion, tomato, 2 drumstick pieces, 1 tbsp tamarind and salt; simmer 10 minutes. Serve.
